summary:
AstroPulse EIMO (Earth-Independent Medical Operations) is an interactive, offline-first clinical decision-support and health monitoring platform engineered for astronauts on deep-space Artemis lunar and Mars missions. When crews travel up to 140 million miles from Earth, communication delays of up to 20 minutes one-way make real-time ground flight-surgeon reliance impossible during acute emergencies or gradual physiological decline.

AstroPulse EIMO addresses the challenge through five integrated modules: (1) a clickable 6-region SVG anatomical body map with color-coded health status and plain-language microgravity exam guides; (2) a multi-modal vitals and diagnostic ultrasound logger (blood pressure, heart rate, blood glucose, core temperature, sleep, mood, hydration, and ocular/renal/cardiac ultrasound); (3) an autonomous emergency triage simulator featuring step-by-step non-physician protocols; (4) dynamic longitudinal trend charts paired with a gamified countermeasure routine; and (5) a Hierarchical Bayesian N-of-1 Digital Twin and 500-trajectory Monte Carlo NASA Integrated Medical Model (IMM) risk simulator. AstroPulse empowers non-physician crews to detect anomalies early, act autonomously, and safeguard human life in deep space.
details:
WHAT IT DOES & HOW IT WORKS
AstroPulse EIMO is an autonomous astronaut health monitoring and clinical triage software platform designed for Earth-Independent Medical Operations (EIMO). It translates complex aerospace medicine into an intuitive visual interface for non-physician astronauts across four mission environments: Space Station (LEO), Spacecraft (Deep Space Mars Transit), Surface Rover (EVA), and Planetary Base (0.16g Moon / 0.38g Mars).

1. Interactive Clickable 6-Zone Anatomical Body Map:
Displays real-time status (Nominal, Caution, Critical) across CNS/Ocular (SANS), Cardiovascular, Renal/Metabolic, Musculoskeletal, Immune/Thermoregulatory, and Behavioral/Circadian systems. Clicking any region explains its physiological function, microgravity risk mechanism, step-by-step non-physician measurement instructions, and escalation rules.

2. Multi-Modal Vitals & Diagnostic Ultrasound Logger:
Ingests blood pressure (mmHg), heart rate (bpm), fasting blood glucose (mg/dL), core body temperature (°C), sleep duration (hrs), ARCHeR mood readiness (1–10), daily hydration (L), and onboard diagnostic imaging (Ocular ONSD ultrasound, Renal flank ultrasound, Parasternal cardiac echo, and Dry Saliva immune assays).

3. Autonomous Emergency Triage Simulator:
Guides crew members step-by-step through five critical spaceflight scenarios—including the halfway-to-Mars acute chest pain and collapse scenario—clearly distinguishing when crew must act immediately onboard versus when to transmit asynchronous Store-and-Forward JSON telemetry packets to Flight Surgeons on Earth.

4. Hierarchical Bayesian N-of-1 Digital Twin & 500-Run Monte Carlo Simulator:
Instead of relying solely on static Earth reference cutoffs, AstroPulse uses conjugate Bayesian updating to fuse NASA Spaceflight Standard Measures (SSM) cohort priors with each astronaut's longitudinal mission history, calculating individualized posterior Z-scores ($Z_{post}$) and Kullback-Leibler divergence ($D_{KL}$). It also models non-linear coupling across NASA's 5 Hazards of Human Spaceflight and runs a 500-trajectory Poisson/Monte Carlo simulation of Total Medical Events (TME), Quality-Adjusted Time Lost (QTL), and evacuation/mortality risk.

5. Longitudinal Trend Charts & Gamified Countermeasure Routine:
Renders zero-dependency native SVG biomarker trend charts across Mission SOLs and gamifies daily ARED resistive exercise, NASA SHOP nutritional targets, and sleep hygiene using XP rewards and mission ranks.

BENEFITS & INTENDED IMPACT
- Spaceflight Impact: Enables autonomous medical survival during deep-space communication blackouts and 20-minute Mars radio delays.
- Earth Dual-Use Impact: Directly transferable to rural telemedicine clinics, polar research stations, submarines, and disaster-response zones operating without immediate hospital access.

TOOLS, CODING LANGUAGES & SOFTWARE USED
- Languages & Frontend: HTML5, CSS3, Tailwind CSS, Vanilla JavaScript (ES6+), TypeScript data schema, and native inline SVG graphics/charting engines for 100% offline reliability with zero external runtime failures.
- Mathematical & Clinical Modeling: Conjugate Gaussian Bayesian N-of-1 updating, Kullback-Leibler divergence, and Poisson/Monte Carlo probabilistic risk simulation grounded in NASA HRP and IMM parameters.

SUPER INTELLIGENCE (SI) DISCLOSURE & METADATA ACKNOWLEDGMENT
In accordance with NASA Space Apps Challenge rules, Super Intelligence (LLM) tools were used to assist in structuring code architecture, mathematical documentation, and UI layout synthesis. No NASA logos, insignia, or restricted branding elements were used or modified.
